state.objective: Resolve an explicit inconsistency in prior Jev outputs and produce the most honest count recommendation. Do not preserve a previous answer for consistency.
facts: 6,908 leaf rows deterministically reduce to 499 unit-free families.
Seventy internal affiliate families and one system-derived current-profit family are deactivate-after-reclassification, leaving a 428-family conservative ceiling.
A proposed design groups the 428 into 142 target placeholders: 58 retain, 63 conditional-merge, 21 unresolved-evidence.
The 21 unresolved placeholders currently stand in for 104 legacy families. Holding those 104 separately produces 225 working accounts.
Large unresolved clusters include 36 Reserve Replacement OE, 36 Replacement OE Expense and 14 Principal liabilities. Evidence may show more than one nature inside each cluster.
Round 1: 142 was defensible if every evidence gate passes (0.86); 225 was best today (0.98).

Round 2: likely range choice favored 200-250 (0.64) over 130-170 (0.36), but another question selected a statement saying use 225 then expect 130-170. These answers conflict on the likely final range.
The user wants the best permutation, but no balances, journals, contracts, policies or subledger reconciliations are available.

definitions.142: Optimistic conditional design if every proposed grouping, including exception placeholders, proves to be a single appropriate nature.
definitions.225: Operational working design: supported merges applied, unresolved legacy families held separately.
definitions.428: No-merger design after confirmed deactivations only.

resolve_conflict.instructions: Which prior count conclusion should control given the unresolved large clusters?

criteria.225_primary: Treat 225 as the primary current recommendation; 142 is an upside compression case, not expected final until evidence supports it.
criteria.142_expected: Treat 142 as the expected final despite evidence likely splitting large clusters.
criteria.428_primary: Reject all supported merges and use 428.

likely_band.instructions: Without transaction evidence, which band is the most defensible planning range rather than an exact promise?

criteria.180_250: A broad 180-250 planning range centered near the 225 working design.
criteria.130_170: A 130-170 range centered near the optimistic 142 design.

lower_bound.instructions: Can 142 be described as a proven lower bound?

criteria.no: Evidence could support a few additional merges or require splits; it is an architecture scenario, not a mathematical bound.
criteria.yes: No valid design can have fewer than 142.

best_today.instructions: If configuration work must start today, which account set should be loaded as the working natural-account design?

criteria.225: Use the 225 working set and mark exception accounts for mandatory resolution before go-live.
criteria.142: Load all 142 and resolve misclassification later.

convergence_rule.instructions: When may 225 accounts be merged toward 142?

criteria.gate_by_gate: Only cluster by cluster after nature, reporting, workflow, opening balance and reconciliation tests pass.
criteria.all_at_once: Immediately because Jev previously called 142 defensible.
criteria.count_target: Whenever needed to meet a target count.

large_cluster_default.instructions: Until evidence is available, how should the 36+36+14 large exception families be configured?

criteria.separate_or_blocked: Keep separately mapped or block posting through controlled suspense/legacy transition; do not assume one nature.
criteria.one_each: Use one account per cluster immediately.

criteria.225_recommended_142_conditional: Recommended working COA is 225; 142 is a conditional optimization scenario; expected production range is currently 180-250 until evidence gates close.

what_is_optimal.instructions: Can the globally best permutation be proven from account labels and Jev judgments alone?

criteria.no: Optimality requires transaction-level and reporting tests; current result is the best evidence-aware candidate set.
